t.1.225.1: Mandapāla said: For the sake of your protection I entreated Jvalana, the blazing Fire, and Agni had already promised beforehand, saying, "So be it."
t.1.225.4: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having thus comforted his sons and taking his wife with him, O Bhārata, Mandapāla then went from that country to another country.
t.1.225.3: You must not grieve over death, my little sons, for even Hutāśa, the Fire, knows you to be seers, and that brahman is known to you.
t.1.225.2: Knowing Agni's word, your mother's knowledge of dharma, and your own supreme valor, I did not come here earlier.
t.1.225.5: The blessed sharp-rayed one too, together with the two Kṛṣṇas, burned the blazing Khāṇḍava forest, bringing about freedom from fear for the world.
t.1.225.6: Having drunk there the streams flowing with marrow and fat, Pāvaka attained supreme satisfaction and revealed himself to Arjuna.
t.1.225.7: Then the blessed lord of the gods, surrounded by the hosts of the Maruts, descended from the sky and spoke these words to Pārtha and Mādhava.
t.1.225.8: This deed has been accomplished by you two, a deed hard to perform even for the immortals. I am pleased; choose boons, even those that are hard to obtain and beyond the reach of men.
t.1.225.9: Pārtha, for his part, chose as his boon to receive all the weapons from Śakra, and Śakra then appointed a time for him to do so.
t.1.225.10: When the blessed Mahādeva has become pleased with you, then I shall give you the weapons meant for the Pāṇḍava, all of them without exception.
t.1.225.11: I myself shall know that time, O joy of the Kurus, and through great austerity I shall give them to you.
t.1.225.12: All the weapons of Agni, and likewise those of Vāyu, and all of mine as well, you shall receive, O Dhanaṃjaya.
t.1.225.13: Vāsudeva too chose as his boon an everlasting friendship with Pārtha, and the lord of the gods, pleased, then granted him that boon.
t.1.225.14: Having granted a boon to the two of them, the lord of the Maruts, pleased, took leave of Hutāśana and went back to heaven together with the gods.
t.1.225.15: And Pāvaka too, having burned that forest together with its beasts and birds for five days and one, ceased, fully satisfied.
t.1.225.16: Having devoured the flesh and drunk the fat and the blood, and filled with the highest delight, he spoke to the two of them, O lord of the people.
t.1.225.17: By you two, foremost among men, I have been satisfied to my heart's content. I give you leave, O heroes; go wherever you desire.
t.1.225.18: Thus those two, Arjuna and Vāsudeva, were given leave by the great-souled Pāvaka, and so too was the Dānava Maya.
t.1.225.19: Then, O bull of the Bharatas, having walked about, all three of them sat down together on the delightful bank of a river.
